requirement:
Each evidence detail page displays its recorded state as a Shields.io static
badge with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body
as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It renders the recorded rationale
as Markdown in a Rationale section and the recorded acknowledgments for FIXME.

Inputs appear once, in the first applicable group: Implementation, Tests,
Referenced definitions, then Other sources. Implementation uses `{impl}`
connections and Tests uses `{test}` connections. Referenced definitions
contains definition inputs and requirement selections wholly covered by the
subject's citations; remaining inputs go to Other sources. Current annotations,
including anchored files, determine these connections
under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Groups are expanded disclosures;
individual inputs are collapsed disclosures identifying their selectors.

An outline input shows its file, selector, kind, current inclusive line range,
and current source text in a fenced code block. A requirements input shows
its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive
line range. Requirements and definition inputs show their recorded text.
The book presents current source alongside the recorded review without
comparing input hashes.

Code fences use Rust highlighting for `.rs` and language-aware highlighting
for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python; TOML may use
INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.index.detail_format` has no structural obligations, and it has no implementation edges. Each clause specifies output that a reader of the rendered page can observe.

- **Badge and body:** "displays its recorded state as a Shields.io static badge with meaningful alt text" and "the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind" describe the rendered page. Any code that emits the same badge, alt text and quote would meet them.
- **Rationale and acknowledgments:** "renders the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and the recorded acknowledgments for FIXME" is also output behavior.
- **Input grouping:** The grouping rules (Implementation, Tests, Referenced definitions, then Other sources) say which inputs appear in which group. They also say that `{impl}` and `{test}` connections, and the subject's citations, decide placement. These are decisions about content. They do not name a library, type, signature or interface. A different internal design could produce the same grouping, so it is discretionary.
- **Disclosures:** Groups are expanded and individual inputs are collapsed. Each input shows its file, selector, kind, line range and source text. These are presentation facts.
- **Highlighting:** "Rust highlighting for `.rs` and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML..." fixes the visible highlighting by language. It does not fix a highlighter library or algorithm.
- **Hashes:** "without comparing input hashes" restricts what the page shows. It does not prescribe how the code is built.
- **Cited requirements:** `requirements.references.roles`, `requirements.references.anchors` and the definition `requirements.references.source_item` supply context for how connections are determined. Their own obligations belong to those requirements.

The `Implements` edges of this requirement are empty, and no review roots were supplied. No root is needed to show a structural obligation, so I found no gap.

behavioral: The marked tests cover every observable obligation of `requirements.index.detail_format`.

- **Badge and alt text.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[detail_page_renders_markdown_and_highlighted_input_sections]` asserts the Shields.io `evidence-Valid-237346` badge. `fn[detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group]` asserts `alt="evidence Recorded true"`. `fn[index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages]` asserts `alt="evidence Missing"`. `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]` asserts the FIXME badge and its alt text.
- **Current body as a block quote labeled by kind.** The tests assert `## Requirement\n\n> Ready MUST work.\n> \n> ## Example` for a requirement and `## Example\n\n> Pending case.` for an example. The recorded stale text is asserted absent. `fn[detail_pages_rebase_markdown_links_and_images_from_the_definition]` checks block-quote rendering of the body.
- **Rationale and FIXME acknowledgments.** `fn[detail_page_renders_markdown_and_highlighted_input_sections]` asserts that the `## Rationale` section renders the recorded rationale as Markdown. `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]` asserts `## FIXME references` and the issue references.
- **Grouping and order.** `fn[detail_inputs_are_grouped_by_current_edges_in_disclosures]` checks the following:
  - The group headings appear in the order Implementation, Tests, Referenced definitions, Other sources, and each input falls inside the expected group.
  - Anchored files (`:impl:` and `:test:`) land in Implementation and Tests.
  - A wholly covered selection goes to Referenced definitions, while a mixed selection (`rules.b*`) goes to Other sources.
  - An example with a `{test}` edge lands in Tests.

  `fn[detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group]` checks that a source with both `{impl}` and `{test}` edges appears once, in Implementation only. It also checks that a definition input lands in Referenced definitions.
- **Disclosures.** Counts of 4 expanded group `<details>` and 9 collapsed input `<details>` are asserted. Input summaries identify the selector, for example `outline src/main.rs fn[main]`.
- **Outline input contents.** `fn[detail_page_renders_markdown_and_highlighted_input_sections]` asserts file, selector, kind, the inclusive range `1–4`, and the current changed source in a fenced block.
- **Requirements and definition inputs.** `fn[detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group]` asserts the selection, each match's full name, file and inclusive range (`md/rules.md:5–7`, `1–3`, `9–13`), and the recorded text. It also checks the unresolved case.
- **No hash comparison in the book.** `fn[book_keeps_recorded_assessments_and_displays_current_source_without_hash_checks]` asserts that the current source is shown and that no stale-hash messages appear. The recorded assessment is kept.
- **Highlighting.** `fn[common_input_extensions_select_highlighting_languages]` asserts the mappings for markdown, json, ini (TOML), java, javascript, typescript and python. The page test asserts that `rust,noplayground`, `markdown` and `ini` fences render.

The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. No obligation is missing evidence.

text: :::{req} detail_format
Each evidence detail page displays its recorded state as a Shields.io static
badge with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body
as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It renders the recorded rationale
as Markdown in a Rationale section and the recorded acknowledgments for FIXME.
Inputs appear once, in the first applicable group: Implementation, Tests,
Referenced definitions, then Other sources. Implementation uses `{impl}`
connections and Tests uses `{test}` connections. Referenced definitions
contains definition inputs and requirement selections wholly covered by the
subject's citations; remaining inputs go to Other sources. Current annotations,
including anchored files, determine these connections
under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Groups are expanded disclosures;
individual inputs are collapsed disclosures identifying their selectors.
An outline input shows its file, selector, kind, current inclusive line range,
and current source text in a fenced code block. A requirements input shows
its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive
line range. Requirements and definition inputs show their recorded text.
The book presents current source alongside the recorded review without
comparing input hashes.
Code fences use Rust highlighting for `.rs` and language-aware highlighting
for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python; TOML may use
INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a {term}`requirements.references.source_item` or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, and needs
no evidence input. Its issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Code implementations are reviewed as part of the definitions they implement or
test. Citation reviews assess cited source items and book passages under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
